paragraphs: Somebody had swapped its feet for wheels again. Yellow Duck Sweater found this out by trying to take a step and gliding instead, across an empty roller rink. Overhead, where a mirror ball belonged, hung the moon, fat and nearly round, one edge missing like a bitten biscuit. Two metres ahead lay the finish line, a strip of silver tape. The duck leaned toward it. The floor leaned the other way. It rolled backwards with great dignity, past a gold coin, a toy rocket and a small jet engine, all sliding downhill beside it, looking embarrassed.

It tried harder, which made things worse. The wheels buzzed, the tape drifted off, and somewhere under the boards the draft of the pit said hello. Bad seed, thought the duck. Zero reward. But it did know one thing about going backwards, because the ring had taught it. So it turned around, pointed its camera eye at the dark end of the rink, and leaned away from the tape. The floor, taken by surprise, tipped. Backwards the duck went, sweater flapping, a small "wheee" escaping before it could stop it. The tape caught across its neck, stretched and snapped, and it kept rolling with two silver ribbons streaming behind it, while the coin, the rocket and the engine came clattering after.

Overhead, where a mirror ball belonged, hung the moon, fat and nearly round, one edge missing like a bitten biscuit. Two metres ahead lay the finish line, a strip of silver tape. The duck leaned toward it. The floor leaned the other way. It rolled backwards with great dignity, past a gold coin, a toy rocket and a small jet engine, all sliding downhill beside it, looking embarrassed.

It tried harder, which made things worse. The wheels buzzed, the tape drifted off, and somewhere under the boards the draft of the pit said hello. Bad seed, thought the duck. Zero reward. But it did know one thing about going backwards, because the ring had taught it. So it turned around, pointed its camera eye at the dark end of the rink, and leaned away from the tape. The floor, taken by surprise, tipped. Backwards the duck went, sweater flapping, a small "wheee" escaping before it could stop it. The tape caught across its neck, stretched and snapped, and it kept rolling with two silver ribbons streaming behind it, while the coin, the rocket and the engine came clattering after.
imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck, with small roller-skate wheels under its orange duck feet, glides wobbling across the polished wooden floor of an empty roller rink at night, while a big, nearly full moon hangs from the ceiling where a mirror ball would be. Panel 2: The duck on its wheels leans its long neck forward toward a strip of silver tape stretched across the rink floor a short way ahead, while the whole floor tilts the other way like a ramp. Panel 3: The duck rolls backwards down the tilted rink floor, away from the silver tape, and beside it a large gold coin, a toy rocket and a small jet engine slide downhill too. Panel 4: The duck has turned around with its back to the silver tape, its camera eye pointed at the dark far end of the rink, leaning its whole body hard away from the tape as the floor begins to tip the other way. Panel 5: The duck speeds backwards on its wheels with its yellow sweater flapping, and the silver tape stretches tight across the back of its thin neck. Panel 6: The duck rolls happily backwards across the moonlit rink with two long silver ribbons streaming from its neck, and the gold coin, the toy rocket and the small jet engine tumble along the floor after it. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
